content:
Apple Books is my favorite reading app, and it's getting some exciting design updates in iOS 27.2. Here's what's new.

Here are the changes iOS 27.2 beta 3 brings to Apple Books

Likely in anticipation of the iPhone Duo being a reading powerhouse, Apple has a slate of design refreshes in store for its Books app.

iOS 27.2 beta 3 introduces these changes, all of which have to do with the reading experience itself.

When reading a book, iOS 27.2 brings the following design updates:

  • New progress bar to track where you are
  • The bottom-right menu now uses a new three-dot icon and has been redesigned as a standard Liquid Glass menu to match other apps
  • The bookmark feature has been removed from that menu and is now a dedicated button in the top-right corner
  • The 'X' button has been moved to the top-left corner
  • The 'back' button has been moved to the bottom-left corner and is now larger than before

These are small updates, but they're definitely welcome improvements in my experience.

I never understood why bookmarking was buried in the old menu, so it's great to see it more visible. I also really appreciate the new progress bar.

I'm hoping that if the iPhone Duo is a hit, Apple will use it as an opportunity to invest more in the Books app. Kindle dominates the e-reader market, but I've always preferred Apple's app and ecosystem for ebooks and audiobooks.

Do you use Apple Books? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.
